approach: In `producer_loop` (producer.rs), after the format step, the replay and the mirror check of each pass, Athena runs the capability's routed checks on the producer's tree with the existing `run_check`, reached through `SnapExec`. `Athena::loop_check_failures` (run/checks.rs) does it in the producer's own build directory (a `Side::Produce` env, so `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` is `target/produce`, no slot link, no second build tree). It takes a build slot only if one is free (`try_acquire`, never waits), runs the disk gate first, and skips the run with a visible `producer   checks not run before the verifier: …` line for a nested or pinned run, an empty change list, a change that holds check-tool configuration, low disk, a busy slot or any error. Only the kill switch leaves the loop (a new `settle_loop_checks` re-reads it after every run, so an advisory step can never abort the job and discard finished work). A failure that is not a timeout and not already failing on the job's base becomes a `CheckFailure`. Each failure adds one problem string to `problems`, which is cloned into `report_problems`, so the stored `self-check failed: …` detail names it and, at the limit, it reaches the verifier as `report_gaps` (flagged, not hidden). The command, exit status and output tail go into the one existing send-back through a new `append_check_failures` in send_back.rs, chained like `append_mirror_drift`. `PRODUCER_SEND_BACKS` stays 1 and no loop is added. So that `git ls-files` in a check lists producer-added files, `ExposedIndex` builds the work tree's index in a temporary file (`GIT_INDEX_FILE` set only for that one `git add -A`, as `Snapshot::work_tree_tree` does), installs it as the snapshot's `.git/index` and restores the saved bytes on drop; `GIT_INDEX_FILE` never goes into a check's environment. Because the in-loop run now executes the configured command for real in `<job>/work`, the test constant `MARKS_BASELINE_OUTSIDE` is changed to touch its mark only when it runs in a `*/baseline` directory, so the CI-reuse tests keep meaning "the baseline ran here".

decisions.choice: 1. Run the in-loop checks in the producer's own build directory with a non-waiting build slot. Build the env with `Side::Produce` (as `format_stage` does, producer.rs:183-194), so `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` is `{job_dir}/target/produce`. `SnapExec` gets `in_loop: bool`; when true it skips the test-only `check_seam`, takes its slot with `SlotQueue::try_acquire` (slots.rs:172-183: never waits, never enqueues; none free gives the plain error `no build slot is free`), and does not call `link_slot_target` or `clean_slot_target`. The timeout is `jc.config.budget.check_timeout_s`, the per-check limit that `format_stage` already passes (producer.rs:199) and that `run_check` enforces (core/src/checks.rs:567-576); the field has no doc comment in config.rs:407, so its meaning here is the one the code gives it.
decisions.reason: A `Side::Verify` env links the build path to the slot's warm target while `target/produce` stays on disk: two full builds at once, which disk.rs:64-67, mod.rs:2008-2011 and CHANGELOG.md:1595-1600 say the checks stage exists to prevent. The producer's cargo wrapper builds in `target/produce` and links no slot target (the only `BuildLink::create` caller is `link_slot_target`, checks.rs:219), so that directory is the warm one for this tree. Verification still removes it first (`free_producer_build`, mod.rs:2011), so disk.rs and the mod.rs comment stay true and are not edited. `try_acquire` keeps the in-loop run from absorbing the slot wait that three existing tests observe at verification: `two_jobs_with_one_build_slot_run_one_after_the_other` (tests.rs:4929, asserts the queued check waited longer), `a_check_that_waited_checks_the_disk_again` (5237) and `a_check_that_waits_past_build_wait_s_holds_the_job` (5292, holds the job after `build_wait_s`). The cost is that a busy slot skips the early feedback. Estimate, not measured: 0% of in-loop attempts when jobs run one at a time, and up to about half when two jobs overlap on the default one slot (`max_check_slots = 1`, athena-data config.rs:165; `[parallel] max_concurrency = 2`, athena.toml:204), because the other job's check run holds the slot for about 1100 s (documented median of 6 runs, docs/design/warm-baseline-build.md:42). D182's Tradeoff says so.

rejected.option: Keep the `Side::Verify` env and the slot's warm target link (round 2)
rejected.why: Two full builds exist during the producer stage, the failure `free_producer_build` removed; it would need disk.rs, mod.rs:2009 and D182 to change the invariant and a new bound test.

rejected.option: Delete `target/produce` before the in-loop run, then rebuild
rejected.why: The producer's next pass starts cold; a send-back pass would rebuild everything.

rejected.option: Call `run_check` directly with a hand-built `CheckContext`, as `format_stage` does
rejected.why: No disk gate, no build slot and no restore of check-made files from the tree (`restore_to(prepared)`).

rejected.option: Take the slot with the queued `acquire(Class::Producer, ..)` as `loop_replay` does (mod.rs:2341) and turn a `SlotWait` into the skip line (critic finding 2, first option)
rejected.why: The wait then happens in the producer stage and verification gets its slot at once, so tests 4929, 5237 and 5292 (and the slot tests in slots.rs and cli slot_exec.rs/drain.rs:3517) would need new fixtures to observe a wait at verification; a second `build_wait_s` is also added to a held job. Named as the follow-up in D182, kept out of this narrow change.

decisions.choice: 2. Skip the in-loop run, with the line `producer   checks not run before the verifier: the change holds check-tool configuration (<paths>), which verification replaces with the base's`, when any changed path satisfies `crate::admission::is_tool_config` (admission.rs:56). The skip line does not start with `checks     `.
decisions.reason: Verification applies the base's tool configuration (`apply_base_tool_config`, verification.rs:472, toolconfig.rs:73) and the producer tree keeps the candidate's. lifecycle.rs:947 has the producer create `.cargo/config.toml` and expects Landed; in the producer tree the cli test check (`! test -f .cargo/config.toml`, common/mod.rs:62) would fail, pass on the base, count as new, spend the one send-back on a fault that does not exist and show the verifier a false gap. The same predicate that verification replaces files by is the skip, so the skip can neither hide a real failure from the verdict nor invent one.

rejected.option: Overlay the base's tool config into the producer tree for the in-loop run
rejected.why: `apply_base_tool_config` needs a two-commit snapshot; the producer's snapshot has one commit and no candidate, so it would need a second implementation and a restore step.

rejected.option: Run anyway and filter the failures
rejected.why: No rule tells which failure is caused by the config file.

decisions.choice: 3. Show producer-added files to `git ls-files` by building the work tree's index in a temporary file (`GIT_INDEX_FILE` set only for that one `git add -A`), copying it over the snapshot's `.git/index` for the length of the in-loop run, and restoring the saved index bytes when the guard `ExposedIndex` is dropped. `GIT_INDEX_FILE` is never put in a check's env. This is a stated departure from the wording of criterion 1 ('GIT_INDEX_FILE set to a temporary index of the work tree'); D182, the changelog bullet and the producer's report record it.
decisions.reason: `run_check` clears the env and then sets `ctx.env` (core/src/checks.rs:532-536), and `Git::command` only adds variables (athena-git/src/lib.rs:233-246), so an exported `GIT_INDEX_FILE` would reach every git process the checks start; Athena's own tests build temp repos with git and would write one shared index whose blobs exist only in the producer's object store. The swap keeps the temporary-index method of `Snapshot::work_tree_tree` (athena-git/src/snapshot.rs:210-218) and still lists new files; a drop guard covers every error path. `work_tree_tree` and `restore_to` use their own temporary index, so the swap does not change them.

rejected.option: Export `GIT_INDEX_FILE` to the check processes
rejected.why: Leaks into the git calls of the tests the checks run; parallel test threads race on one index and commits fail on missing blobs.

rejected.option: `git add -A` into the snapshot's real index and leave it
rejected.why: Leaves staged changes in the producer's repository for its next pass and its own `git status`.

rejected.option: Run the checks in a committed two-commit snapshot like `verifier_snapshot`
rejected.why: The candidate commit does not exist inside the loop, and a second full copy of the tree per pass costs disk and time.

decisions.choice: 4. Run every routed, non-skipped check in config order and send back each new failure: failed, not timed out (`checks::timed_out`, core/src/checks.rs:481), and not pre-existing on the base (`verify::is_pre_existing`, verify.rs:203, with the baseline kept only when `base_commit == ctx.prediction`, through a helper `baseline_for` also used at mod.rs:2127-2130). The loop calls `exec` per item itself, because `routing::run_local` stops after the first failure (routing.rs:181). A low disk, a busy slot or any error ends the run with the skip line and returns the failures found so far (they are collected into an out-parameter).
decisions.reason: One repair pass can then fix fmt, clippy and test together. Verification holds a job whose only new failures timed out (mod.rs:2144) and leaves pre-existing failures out of the verdict, so a send-back for either would make the producer chase a fault it cannot fix.

rejected.option: Stop at the first failing check
rejected.why: Spends the one send-back on one fault and leaves later checks to fail at verification.

rejected.option: Send back every non-passing check
rejected.why: Spends the send-back on timeouts and base failures that the verdict ignores.

decisions.choice: 5. Render with `append_check_failures(text, &[CheckFailure])` in send_back.rs, chained after `append_mirror_drift` and `append_missing_changelog` at producer.rs:639. It inserts a leading sentence after the last `## Sent back` heading and closes with each check's name, command, exit status and output tail (at most 3000 bytes each, via `checks::tail`).
decisions.reason: Later send-back additions use this shape (send_back.rs:219-267). The intro of `send_back_text_scoped` speaks only of criteria (send_back.rs:161-172), so a leading sentence is needed. The four `send_back_text*` wrappers and their callers stay unchanged. `run_check` already redacts the tail (core/src/checks.rs:631).

rejected.option: Add a `checks` parameter to `send_back_text_scoped` and its three wrappers
rejected.why: Touches every wrapper and call site for no gain over the append pattern.

decisions.choice: 6. Run the in-loop checks on every pass, including the second, and put a one-line summary of each failure in both `problems` and `report_problems`. The loop never calls `ctx.stages.enter(.., Stage::Checks)`. The reused field is `Reported.report_gaps`, kept at producer.rs:312-314 as 'What the last report still lacked after the send-back'; it is a free `Vec<String>` that verification.rs:100-112 turns into the `producer-report-gaps` entry the verifier reads as flagged items, which is what criterion 2 needs (the entry names a still-failing check; it is not itself a check).
decisions.reason: A check still failing after the send-back must reach the verifier as flagged (criterion 2): `report_problems` becomes `report_gaps` (producer.rs:576-583). Not entering `Stage::Checks` keeps the stage order that lifecycle.rs:1589 pins.

rejected.option: Run only on the first pass
rejected.why: A check still failing, or a fix that breaks another check, would not be flagged.

decisions.choice: 7. Do not edit docs/decision-links.toml, athena-git, disk.rs or the reader and verifier prompts. D182 is worded without `amends`, `supersedes` or `superseded` and says D115 and D156 stand.
decisions.reason: The only `[[governs]]` entry is D08, for athena-git/src/snapshot.rs and run/candidate.rs (decision-links.toml:219-224); neither is touched, so the decision gate asks for nothing, and criterion 7 asks for a link only when the entry amends or supersedes an earlier one.

rejected.option: Add an `amended` link from D115
rejected.why: D115 (recorded checks on the same tree count as evidence) is applied here, not revised.

decisions.choice: 8. Each test that claims 'the in-loop check ran' proves it with a marker file. The check command (built with the existing `leaked_sh_check`, tests.rs:4363) first appends `$PWD target=$CARGO_TARGET_DIR index=${GIT_INDEX_FILE:-unset} new=<yes|no>` to a file in the test's own temp directory. The producer's tree is `<job_dir>/work` (state.rs:101-102), the baseline's `<job_dir>/baseline` (checks.rs:562) and the verifier's `<job_dir>/verify` (mod.rs:1978), so a line whose path ends in `/work` is an in-loop run.
decisions.reason: A check guarded by `if test -f NEW.txt` passes with producer count 1 whether or not the in-loop run happened, so the count alone proves nothing. The marker proves the run happened on the producer's tree, in `target/produce`, with no `GIT_INDEX_FILE`, and (for the new-file tests) saw `NEW.txt`. A negative twin at the guard level, `the_exposed_index_lists_new_files_and_is_restored_on_drop`, shows `git ls-files` does not list the file without the guard.

rejected.option: A UI line on every successful in-loop run
rejected.why: Many athena-cli and core tests compare UI line sequences; a new line in every job's output is a wide change for a test aid.

rejected.option: Read a marker under the snapshot's `.git/` after `go`
rejected.why: The work tree is removed when the job's run ends, so the file is gone.

decisions.choice: 9. Only the kill switch leaves the in-loop step as an error (answers finding 3). `loop_check_failures` is a wrapper: it runs `run_loop_checks(.., &mut found)` and then `settle_loop_checks(ui, ran)`, which first calls `self.refuse_if_stopped()?` (so a kill during a check, which `run_check` reports as a failed run with the note 'killed by the kill switch', core/src/checks.rs:577-579, ends the job before any send-back) and then turns an `Err` into the line `producer   checks not run before the verifier: <text>` and `Ok(())`. The text uses `LowDisk::text()` or the plain message, not `Display` (which says 'the job stays queued', disk.rs:128-135). The wrapper returns the failures found so far.
decisions.reason: mod.rs:1820-1826 returns any error from `producer_loop` before `candidate_stage`, so an I/O error in an advisory run (`work_tree_tree`, `restore_to`, the index swap, the registry) would discard the producer's finished work, though verification would judge it. `loop_replay` (mod.rs:2293) follows the same rule: 'Only the kill switch is an error'. `refuse_if_stopped` (lib.rs:301) returns a plain `bail!` with no type, so the wrapper re-reads the switch instead of matching a type. A unit test drives `settle_loop_checks` with an arbitrary error and with the stop file set (the stop file path pattern of tests.rs:665-680).

rejected.option: Propagate every error from the in-loop run
rejected.why: An advisory step could end the job and drop a finished candidate.

rejected.option: Convert the kill switch to a skip line too
rejected.why: The job would carry on after `athena stop`.

decisions.choice: 10. Because the in-loop `SnapExec` skips `check_seam` and runs the configured command for real in `<job>/work`, change the test constant `MARKS_BASELINE_OUTSIDE` (tests.rs:6837) from `touch ../../baseline-ran` to `case "$(pwd)" in */baseline) touch ../../baseline-ran;; esac`, and say in its doc comment that the mark is made only by the baseline run. Audit result of every check command the core and cli tests configure is in dependents (answers finding 1).
decisions.reason: `touch ../../baseline-ran` run in `<job>/work` creates `<state>/jobs/baseline-ran`, the file `baseline_ran` reads (tests.rs:6814-6820), so `baseline_reused_from_the_landed_candidates_run_runs_nothing_locally` (6918, asserts at 6945), 6966 (6988), 7025 (7041) and `baseline_waits_for_mains_in_progress_run_then_reuses_it` (7116, asserts at 7131) would fail on `assert!(!run.baseline_ran)`. With the case guard the baseline run (in `<job>/baseline`) still makes the mark, so the tests that assert `baseline_ran` is true (7054, 7147, 7176, 7208, 7322, 7346) keep their meaning and none is weakened.

rejected.option: Let the in-loop `SnapExec` honour `check_seam`
rejected.why: The fake's `executed` list would gain in-loop entries and the CI-reuse tests that assert which checks the local executor was asked (for example `ci_reuse_green_skips_local_checks`, 7364) would fail; the seam also fakes results the in-loop tests need to be real.

rejected.option: A test-only switch that turns the in-loop run off
rejected.why: It would hide the behavior the tests must show and add a production branch for tests.

decisions.choice: 11. Name the added wall time and the follow-up in D182, and do not change the verification run (answers finding 4). Estimate (labelled, not measured for the in-loop run): one in-loop run is about one check run, a median of 1107 s (range 953 to 1248 s, n = 6, fmt + clippy + test, docs/design/warm-baseline-build.md:42), less where `target/produce` is warm (the compile share is unmeasured, warm-baseline-build.md:121); a job sent back once pays two runs, about 37 minutes at that median. Each check keeps its `check_timeout_s` bound (1800 s, athena.toml:52). Proposed follow-up, kept out of this change: reuse a passing in-loop result at verification when the tree fingerprint and the tool configuration are unchanged (D115 already treats recorded checks on the same tree as evidence), and a queued slot wait for the in-loop run.
decisions.reason: Reuse would touch the verification path, the baseline filter and the fingerprint rules, which is a second change with its own tests; the request is only that the producer sees the failure before the verdict.

rejected.option: Reuse the in-loop result at verification in this change
rejected.why: Needs the verification path, the fingerprint and a new record of an in-loop run; not narrow, and the planner deadline of the previous attempt came from over-wide plans.
